Title: Understanding Multiplication as Equal Groups
Objectives: Interpret products as total objects in equal groups
Create real-world contexts for multiplication expressions
Use arrays/drawings to represent multiplication scenarios
Key Concepts: Interpret products as total objects in equal groups (e.g., 5 × 7 means 5 groups of 7)
Create real-world contexts for multiplication expressions
Use arrays/drawings to represent multiplication scenarios

Teaching Steps.Content: Let’s start with a fun activity! I’ll show you a picture of some groups of objects—like 3 groups of 4 apples each. Can you count how many apples there are in total? (Show image.) Yes, it’s 12! Today, we’ll learn how multiplication helps us quickly find totals like this.

Multiplication is like adding the same number over and over. For example, 4 × 3 means 4 groups of 3. Let’s draw it: (Draw on board: OOO OOO OOO OOO). How many circles total? (12!) That’s right—4 groups of 3 is 12. Now, you try: What’s 2 × 5? Draw it on your paper!

Where do we see equal groups in real life? (Pause for ideas.) Like 6 packs of juice with 2 bottles each—how many bottles? (6 × 2 = 12)! Now, pair up and invent your own multiplication story. For example, 'If I have 5 bags with 8 marbles each…'

Let’s represent 3 × 4 as an array of dots: 3 rows of 4 dots each. (Demonstrate on grid paper.) This shows rows and columns, just like seats in our classroom! Now, you make an array for 5 × 2. How many dots? (10!)
Today, we learned that multiplication is about equal groups. 4 × 3 isn’t just 12—it’s 4 groups of 3! We drew arrays, made up stories, and even saw it in real life. Tomorrow, we’ll practice even more!

Group Discussion Questions: Your teacher has 7 baskets. Each basket holds 6 oranges. How many oranges are there in total? Draw an array or equal groups to show your work!
